description: Work out, for each record class in a company's own retention schedule, the date it must be kept through and the first day it may be destroyed. Send each class with its creation date and the retention years (and months) the schedule says, and optionally a date to check against (as_of), whether the count starts at the creation date, the end of that month or the end of that year, and whether the class is permanent or on legal hold. Get back, for every class, the keep-through date, the earliest destruction date and, if you sent as_of, whether it is still to be kept, eligible for destruction, on hold or permanent, with the days left. The retention years are yours: the tool does not know what the law requires. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/retention-schedule-dates). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

as_of.description: Optional: the date to check each class against (usually today), YYYY-MM-DD.

records.description: Record classes with creation date and retention period (1 to 200).

created.description: Creation date of the record or of the batch, YYYY-MM-DD.

legal_hold.description: true when a legal hold, audit or open dispute stops destruction for this class (you decide that; the dates are still worked).

permanent.description: true when your schedule keeps this class permanently (no destruction date).

record_class.description: Your name for the record class, for example 'vendor contracts' (your own text, echoed; not a person's name).

retention_months.description: Extra months on top of the years (0 to 11, default 0).

retention_years.description: Whole years your schedule says to keep this class (0 to 100). Leave out only when permanent is true.

start_from.description: Where the count starts: creation_date (default), the last day of the creation month, or 31 December of the creation year.
